title: Main Vaapas Aaunga Arrives June 12. Imtiaz Ali Has Reunited A.R. Rahman and Irshad Kamil for a Partition Love Story. This Is Not a Drill.
excerpt: Diljit Dosanjh, Naseeruddin Shah, Sharvari, and Vedang Raina star in what might be Bollywood's most emotionally loaded release of the summer — and Rahman just debuted the music at the Attari Border.
body:
The first artist to ever perform at the Attari Border did it on a Sunday afternoon, standing where the Indian flag descends every evening at sunset. **A.R. Rahman** — two Oscars, a Grammy, a Padma Bhushan — played to an audience of BSF jawans and film crew, opening with *Chanda Suraj Lakhon Taare* before tearing through the songs of **Main Vaapas Aaunga**, and closing, inevitably, with *Maa Tujhe Salaam*.

The concert was beautiful. It was also the most extravagant trailer launch of the year. Because the film it belongs to — **Imtiaz Ali**'s partition-era love story starring **Diljit Dosanjh**, **Naseeruddin Shah**, **Sharvari**, and **Vedang Raina** — arrives in theatres on June 12, and everything about it feels like a filmmaker betting his entire career on a single emotional frequency.

## Two Love Stories, Eighty Years Apart

The premise spans nearly a century. In pre-Partition India, a soft-spoken aspiring poet named Keenu (**Vedang Raina**) falls for Jiya (**Sharvari**), a young woman who is more decisive than he will ever be. Their romance blooms in the undivided Punjab of the 1940s — and then 1947 arrives, and the border that Rahman performed at this afternoon cuts their world in half.

Eighty years later, an elderly Keenu (**Naseeruddin Shah**) wants to cross that border one last time. He wants to go home — to the town that is now in Pakistan, to the house where he was young and in love. His grandson (**Diljit Dosanjh**) is the one trying to make it happen.

> "This is such a unique event. No artist has performed at the Attari border before. And isn't it magical that this is happening around Main Vaapas Aaunga, a film that is based on Partition, and the stories of love and longing?" — Imtiaz Ali

## The Band Is Back Together

This is a reunion that matters. Imtiaz Ali, A.R. Rahman, and lyricist **Irshad Kamil** last worked as a trio on *Tamasha* (2015). Before that, they gave us *Rockstar*, *Highway*, and *Jab We Met*. Every one of those films lived or died by its music, and every one of them is still on your playlist. The fact that they have come back together for this — a story about borders, loss, and a love that survives a country splitting in two — tells you something about the weight of the material.

**Mohit Chauhan** returns to sing alongside newcomers Pooja Tiwari and Nargis. The track *Maskara*, performed live by Vedang Raina and Nilanjana Ghosh at Attari, is already generating early buzz. *Ishq Mastana*, with Chauhan's unmistakable vocal warmth, feels like the spiritual successor to *Tum Se Hi* — the kind of song that soundtracks a generation's idea of romance.

## Why This One Hits Different for the Diaspora

Partition films are not new. But a Partition film starring Diljit Dosanjh — the biggest Punjabi crossover star on the planet, currently mid-sold-out-arena-tour — released in a month where diaspora audiences are already in theatres for Peddi and Hai Jawani? That is new.

The film is set for wide international release. For NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada — many of whom are Punjabi families with their own Partition stories handed down through grandparents — this is not just entertainment. It is personal archaeology. The fact that Imtiaz Ali chose to launch the music at the actual border, the physical line that the story revolves around, is the kind of gesture that turns a film into an event.

The supporting cast includes **Rajat Kapoor**, **Manish Chaudhary**, and **Anjana Sukhani**. The film is produced by **Birla Studios** and **Applause Entertainment**, with **Window Seat Films**' Mohit Choudhary and Shibasish Sarkar.

## The Competition Is Brutal

June 12 is not a solo release. **Main Vaapas Aaunga** lands alongside Manoj Bajpayee's **Governor**, Kangana Ranaut's **Bharat Bhhagya Vidhaata**, and **Haunted 3D: Echoes of the Past**. Four films, one Friday, in a month that already has ₹1,400 crore at stake. Trade analysts have called it suicidal. Imtiaz Ali seems unbothered.

He might be right to be. The film has something none of the others do: Rahman's music, a story that makes you cry just reading the synopsis, and Diljit Dosanjh's face on the poster. In the current Bollywood landscape, that combination is less a release strategy and more a prayer — but it is a prayer backed by two Oscar wins, a legendary director, and four actors at the top of their game.

**Main Vaapas Aaunga** releases in theatres worldwide on June 12, 2026. Music is on Tips Music.
author: Diaspora Desk
